scope: read-only review and tests on temporary SQLite stores; no queue-v3 integration, production store, scientific job or model run

reproduction.author_suite_result: 13 tests passed in 0.380 seconds in this review; the 12 simultaneous race samples again all had seal win, while explicit held-order tests covered both serializations.
targeted_output: first_finalize OSError simulated interruption after temp fsync

confirmed_properties: The serialized enqueue/seal operations share the same flock and BEGIN IMMEDIATE database transaction; tests cover enqueue-first and seal-first orders, and both produce the intended membership and state.
Pre/post SQLite commit process exits behave as documented in the temporary fixture. Sealed membership and exact accepted retry persist after commit; new admission rejects after seal.

Final row bytes are committed before filesystem projection, and retry validates and projects the same bytes. Tested explicit-empty and terminal-with-failure dispositions remain clearly distinct from success/qualification.

The core expressly does not integrate V3 admission intents, executor reconciliation, dependency/liveness evidence, or scientific qualification. The report does not support production or thousands-cycle claims.

blocker.name: same-process retry can be permanently blocked by stale pid-named receipt temp
blocker.source: core.py project(): temporary path is receipt-<run>-<os.getpid()>.tmp and is opened with xb; failures before unlink leave it behind.
blocker.counterexample: Create and seal an explicit-empty run, inject an ordinary OSError at receipt_before_publish after the temporary file has been fsynced, restore the fault, and call finalize again from the same process. The first call has already committed FINALIZED; the retry raises FileExistsError because the first temp file remains and the pid is unchanged.
blocker.impact: This is an ordinary API exception/retry case, distinct from same-user forgery and from process-crash recovery where the next process usually has a different PID. It contradicts unconditional retryability after publication-stage failure. It also can recur after a real crash if a PID is reused before stale temp cleanup.
blocker.smallest_fix: Use a collision-resistant per-attempt exclusive temporary name (e.g. random nonce plus pid) so a stale inert temp cannot block a retry; optionally clean only the current attempt's temp in a finally block when safe. Keep exclusive final publication and exact-byte verification. Add same-process injected-error retry, stale-PID temp, and crash-restart tests.

remaining_limits: The tests assume honest local Linux filesystems and cooperating writers; they do not prove power-loss/device-flush durability, network-filesystem semantics, malicious coherent SQLite rewrites or immutable evidence.
The injected test seam exercises process exits at enumerated points; it does not establish all kernel/storage failure behavior.

A production adapter still must atomically own partial admission before scaffolding and integrate actual queue-v3 reconciliation under its authoritative lock. The core alone does not fix the previously identified V3 enqueue/seal race.
